unmapped: Objective is quickest change detection: minimise expected detection delay E[(tau-nu)^+] subject to a false-alarm constraint P^infty[tau < m] <= alpha; the learner chooses both a sensing action and a stopping time
Single abrupt change at unknown time nu from a known pre-change parameter theta_0 to an unknown post-change parameter theta* in a known set Theta^(1)
The learner knows theta_0, Theta^(1) and the observation distributions P_theta(.|a) for every action
settings.definition_quote:
At each decision round $t$, the parameter $	heta_t$ governs the distribution of the observation taken in that round. Let $
u$ denote the round at which the change in behavior occurs, so that $	heta_t = 	heta_0$ for $t < 
u$ and $	heta_t = 	heta^* \in \ThetaOne$ for $t \geq 
u$. At each round $t$, a learner decides to either (1) stop and output that a change has taken place, ... or (2) continue ... and play an action or sensing decision $A_t$ from an action set $\mathcal{A}$. ... The learner is aware, a priori, of the pre-change parameter $	heta_0$, the post-change parameter set $\ThetaOne$ and the observation distribution structure

symbols.m_fa: false alarm time horizon m (P^infty[tau < m] <= alpha)
symbols.D_star: max_a KL(theta*(a) || theta_0(a)), divergence of the most informative action

source.label: thm:lowerbound
source.quote: Let $0 < \alpha \leq \frac{1}{10}$ and $m \geq 1$. For any bandit changepoint algorithm satisfying $\probSup{(\infty)}{\tau < m} \leq \alpha$, we have $\mathbb{E}^{(1, \theta^*)}\left[\tau \right] \geq \min \left\{ \frac{\frac{1}{20} \log \frac{1}{\alpha}}{\max_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \kl{\theta^*(a)}{\theta^{(0)}(a)}}, \frac{m}{2} \right\} \quad \forall \theta^* \in \ThetaOne$.

results.notes: Bound on expected stopping time (detection delay with nu=1). Algorithm class: all detectors satisfying the (m,alpha) false alarm constraint.

conditions: algorithm satisfies P^infty[tau < nu + m | nu <= tau] <= alpha

source.label: thm:epsgreedygenchange
source.quote: (Time to false alarm) Let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}$. If the stopping threshold $\beta$ is set as $\beta \geq \frac{m \SizeThetaOne}{\alpha}$, then the stopping time satisfies $\probInf{\tau < m} \leq \alpha$.

results.notes: False-alarm guarantee: probability of stopping before m under no change is at most alpha (proof gives m|Theta^(1)|/beta). Quantity mapped to error_probability.

source.quote: Consider the limiting situation as $\alpha \rightarrow 0$ and $m = \omega\left(\log \frac{1}{\alpha} \right) \to \infty$. Then, any admissible change detector in ${\cal D}_{m,\alpha}$ must suffer $$\liminf_{\alpha \to 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}^{(\nu,\theta^*)}[(\tau-\nu)^+]}{ \log\frac{1}{\alpha}} \geq \frac{1}{\max_{a} D({\theta^*(a)}||{\theta^{(0)}(a)})}.$$

results.notes: Informal theorem; the constant 1 differs from the 1/20 in the formal Theorem 2, so it is stated informally and may not exactly follow from the formal results.

conditions: alpha -> 0, m = omega(log(1/alpha)), log m = o(log(1/alpha))

source.quote: On the other hand, the $\epsilon$-GCD algorithm, suitably tuned to be in ${\cal D}_{m,\alpha}$, achieves $$\limsup_{\alpha \to 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}^{(\nu,\theta^*)}[(\tau-\nu)^+]}{ \log\frac{1}{\alpha}} \leq \frac{8}{(1-\epsilon)} \frac{1}{\max_{a} D({\theta^*(a)}||{\theta^{(0)}(a)}) }.$$

results.notes: Informal theorem; asymptotic consequence of Theorem 4. Expression written as c*log(1/alpha) per convention.
